sections.heading: C — Some Special Driving Situations
sections.markdown:
## C — Some Special Driving Situations

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
Night driving runs far deadlier with weaker sight, so daylight trips beat night runs and tired drivers stay parked, night speeds drop inside headlight range, lamps burn from thirty minutes after sunset to thirty minutes before sunrise or under one-thousand-foot visibility, and eyes shift low-right against oncoming glare [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
Low beams take over within five hundred feet of oncoming cars, within three hundred feet behind leaders, on lit roads, and in fog, rain, sleet, snow, or dust, while night-parked cars on dark highways keep parking or low beams lit [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
Texas highways span the maintained public width between boundary lines, trips pre-plan entrances, directions, and exits with fit drivers and cars skipping roads above their minimum pace, and entries yield to highway traffic through right-side speed-change lanes with left signals and merging speed [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A02
Highway lanes assign right to minimum-or-slower pace, middle and left to faster travel and passing, and early exits to prompt lane moves, then demand centered steady pacing without weaving, two-second gaps stretching to four in weather with sudden-stop readiness, merger room, and faster-traffic passing room from non-right lanes [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A02
Exits claim their lane early and earlier in heavy traffic with signs posted at least one thousand yards out, then slow along ramps into the lower limit [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A02
Highway hypnosis from drone and monotony yields to stops every two hours or one hundred miles with walks, eight-hour driving days, roaming eyes on signs and mirrors, open-window air, daytime-only sunglasses, blind-spot avoidance by hanging back or passing through, and phones parked for pull-overs or hands-free use with under-eighteen use banned outside emergencies [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A02
Breakdowns move everyone off roads that trap cars with warning devices out, roll stricken cars off pavement even on flats, flash emergency and tail lamps plus cabin lights at night, and fly white cloths or raised hoods [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A03
Every emergency obeys think-before-you-act, so skids meet lifted gas pedals instead of slammed brakes, steering into the slide, and gentle straightening, with prevention via slower poor-condition driving and sound-tread tires [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A03
Brake failure answers with calm parking-brake plus lower-gear slowing short of lockup, pavement departures answer with gripped wheels, lifted gas, careful braking, and slowed checked re-entry, flats and blowouts answer with lifted gas, gentle brakes, and straight stops, and steep descents answer with low gears and never neutral or clutch coasting [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A03
Winter widen gaps against icy rear-enders since snow tires still slide, admits no safe snow-or-ice speed, bans brake-locking, clears windows with working wipers and defrosters, suspects bridge ice, shady melt delays, and turns, starts gently with brake tests and pre-turn slowing, and trusts chains most while denying them normal-speed security [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A04
Modern roundabouts circle one-way counterclockwise under yield signs with eight conflict points against thirty-two at signalized four-ways, driven by slowing, yielding to circling traffic, counterclockwise entry, and signaled right exits, with single lanes heeding advisory speeds and bike-or-pedestrian crossings, multi-lanes obeying advance lane signs without in-circle changes, big rigs granted room, and emergency pull-overs kept to approaches and exits rather than inside [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A04
Nearly half of flash-flood deaths involve vehicles. Six inches reaches the underside of most passenger cars, causing lost control and possible stalling; twelve inches floats many cars. Two feet of rushing water can sweep away pickups, SUVs and most other vehicles. Floodwater may conceal missing roadbed or a bridge, and weakened roads may collapse under a vehicle after water recedes. Leave a stalled vehicle quickly for higher ground; avoid flooded routes by choosing another way. A vehicle floats when buoyancy exceeds its weight. Modern roundabouts reduce severe intersection crashes by an average of eighty percent [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A05
Trucks brake and accelerate slower, swing wider, and weigh more, so passes check fronts, rears, mirrors, and blind spots for clear legal zones, flash headlights especially at night while trucks hold far sides, budget three to five extra seconds level with easier climbs and harder descents, finish fast without lingering, and return only on truck light-flashes with full truck fronts mirrored while holding speed [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A05
Passed drivers drift far-side, ease speed, never accelerate, and heed truck return signals, oncoming meetings hug far sides against sideswipes since turbulence pushes apart, following respects two-hundred-forty-foot car stops against four-hundred-plus-foot loaded rig stops at fifty-five miles per hour, rear blind spots stay empty with drivers visible in truck side mirrors, night lights dim against mirror glare, and uphill stops leave rollback room on the left for visibility [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A05
Truck right turns swing wide past deceptive right-side gaps that passing cars must avoid, backing trucks block roads that waiting cars must respect from outside blind spots, center-lane cruising aids merges and escape options, cutoffs steal safety cushions with construction-zone races worst of all, and big size masks true truck speed at intersections [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A06
Motorcyclists share full road rights, yet half of bike crashes involve other vehicles and riders die about thirty-five times more often, hidden by car-seeking eyes, tiny profiles, tricky distance judgment, constant lane shifts, and distraction, with left turns across their path most deadly plus blind spots, surface hazards, wind gusts, and large-vehicle blocking [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A06
Bike-aware drivers double-check intersections especially before lefts, signal every lane move since bike signals rarely self-cancel and flashing liars must prove their turns, and grant full lane widths without sharing [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A07
Followers trail bikes four to six seconds back and a full car length at stops against rear-end shoves, remembering dry bikes outbrake cars, while the training program born in nineteen eighty-three and moved from DPS to licensing regulators in twenty twenty spends fee money on rider skills, and quiet street light rail demands never occupying tracks, crossing only designated spots both ways under all signals, listening for horns and bells, and never racing, beating, or circling gates [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A08
Bicycles count as vehicles with full rights and duties, ride beyond right lanes on one-way multi-lane streets and car-pathed left turns, earn motorist merges on right turns without cut-across moves, hug right only in safely shareable lanes, claim full lanes to pass, turn left, dodge hazards, or survive narrow lanes, and crash most when cars left-hook oncoming riders, right-hook their paths, or pull from stops across their right-of-way [A08] [A07].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A08
Distraction steals eyes, hands, or minds from driving until gazes miss plain sights, triggered by texting, passengers, stereos, food, reading, retrievals, billboards, gawking, phones, telematics, and daydreams, doubling crashes on half-second delays, fought by pre-learning devices, pre-setting stations and media, decluttering, pre-planning routes, pre-setting mirrors, banning in-motion reading and texting, skipping smoke and meals, and cooling intense talks, while others' drifting, speed swings, object fumbling, and chatting earn extra room and careful passes [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A08
Texting law bans reading, writing, and sending on portable wireless devices with fines on conviction, ignores ringing phones, allows law-enforcement and emergency calls, and otherwise pulls cars off roads for short or passenger-placed calls [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0060]

items.why: Section Nine is procedure recall served by standard flashcards and quizzes; no separate practice mode is needed.

corpus_stability.reason: The Texas Driver Handbook is a periodically revised official edition, so Section Nine situation rules change at most with new editions.
